worksheet.title: Follow the Arrows
worksheet.subtitle: Follow the steps to find Bit's box
worksheet.learning_goal: I can follow arrow steps in order to find where Bit lands.

parts.title: Follow the steps in order
parts.text: Each ➡ moves Bit one box to the right. Follow the arrows in order, one box at a time, to see where Bit lands. The star is on box 4.

parts.title: Two steps
parts.prompt: Bit starts on box 1 and follows ➡ ➡. Which box does Bit land on? Write the box number.

parts.title: Four steps
parts.prompt: Bit starts on box 1 and follows ➡ ➡ ➡ ➡. Which box does Bit land on? Write the box number.

parts.title: You try — land on the star
parts.prompt: Bit starts on box 2 and follows ➡ ➡. Which box does Bit land on? Is it the star? Write the box number.

parts.title: Big idea
parts.text: Following steps in order, one at a time, is how you run an algorithm. Computers follow their steps exactly the same way.

parts.title: What this worksheet teaches
parts.text: Children carry out a list of right arrows on the numbered boxes and report the box Bit lands on. Following step-by-step directions in order is running a plan — the number of steps decides the result. No coding experience needed.

parts.title: Before you start (no computer needed)
parts.text: No computer — paper and a pencil or crayon. You read each prompt aloud. Optional: tape a row of numbered boxes (and a star) on the floor so a child can walk the steps.

parts.title: How to lead it (about 15 minutes)
text: 1. Show them (you do). Start on box 1, do three right arrows one at a time → box 4 (the star).
2. Do one together. Exercise 1 — start 1, two arrows → box 3.
3. Let them try. Children do Exercise 2 (four arrows → box 5) and Exercise 3 (start 2, two arrows → box 4).

parts.title: Answer key (these are the verified correct answers)
text: Exercise 1 — start 1, two right arrows → box 3. Exercise 2 — start 1, four right arrows → box 5.
Exercise 3 — start 2, two right arrows → box 4 (yes, the star).

parts.title: If children get stuck — and ways to adjust
text: Watch for: starting the count from the wrong box. Put a finger on the start box first.
Make it easier: walk each arrow on the floor boxes, pausing on each number.
Make it harder: ask which start box lands on the star with three arrows.
Make it active: call the arrows aloud while a child steps the boxes.

parts.title: Ontario Kindergarten link (official wording)
text: Problem Solving and Innovating — children follow a sequence of directional instructions.
In plain terms: carrying out a list of steps in order to see where Bit ends up.
No reading is needed from the child — you read each prompt aloud; the child answers by circling, numbering, or drawing arrows.

parts.title: You'll know it worked when
parts.text: The child follows the arrows in order and writes the correct landing box each time.
